newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail, truck offers fall again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail, truck offers fall again.

text.p: Some soymeal rail and truck offers fell further Thursday in response to a drop in soybean basis bids and stout supplies in some markets, dealers said.
"Basis is just crumbling," said one dealer in Minnesota. "There's also some meal around for sale."
Dealers reported only small trades in the spot market early Thursday and said end-users were still reluctant to book soymeal for forward delivery at current prices.
As of 1040 CDT, August soymeal was up $5.60 at $259.50 per ton, and other contracts were $4.20 to $6.30 higher.
Most trade sources were looking for the weekly crush from that National Oilseed Processors Association to exceed last week's pace of 23.891 million bushels.
Estimates ranged from 22.70 to 24.20 million bushels, but most said a recent improvement in crushing margins would push the crush up near 24.00 million.
"I suppose there are some decent margins, so that should dictate an increase in the crush," a dealer in Indiana said.
